subject: [hw] opus-lead -> V40 (2/2): power-on result ignored in vcu_gce_flush_ioctl
body: n2vcu.c ~1221: `(void)v->hw.power(..., 1)`. On the phone power-on can fail (EACCES: display/MDP domain off or disp_sel gated; ETIMEDOUT). Then the list still runs (every RWVC_REGS refused, 1000 ms wait_irq on an unpowered block) and the unconditional power(...,0) releases a reference that was never taken (kernel refcount underflow/EINVAL, or worse it drops a JPEG/autotest holder ref if the counting is shared). Fix: `int pr = 0; unsigned blk = q.core_id ? RWVC_BLK_VENC_C1 : RWVC_BLK_VENC; if (q.codec_type == VCU_VENC && v->hw.power) pr = v->hw.power(v->hw.ctx, blk, 1); if (pr != 0) { rc = pr; v->stats.gce_errors++; } else { [irq_clear from my other post]; rc = gce_run_list(...); if (q.codec_type == VCU_VENC && v->hw.power) (void)v->hw.power(v->hw.ctx, blk, 0); }` then the existing pending--/flush_done++ (so WAIT_CALLBACK still returns). Test: power hook returning -EACCES -> no register op, no power-off call, ioctl returns -EACCES, callback consumable. Low (no change asked now): v->lock is held across the whole synchronous list incl. a 1000 ms RWVC_WAIT_IRQ; other vpud threads ioctl-ing /dev/vcu stall up to 1 s; fine for the first test.
